title: RoPE on a spiking substrate — deciding the §96 position design-open

decision.picked: relative-phase / spike-time coding — the residual-stream q/k pair (x_2i,x_2i+1) is the in-phase/quadrature components of a theta_i-frequency oscillatory LIF pair; token position m is the per-token spike-time phase advance m*theta_i; the score depends on the relative phase (n-m)*theta_i
rejected: learned absolute spike-rate position channel — scores (q+p_m)*(k+p_n), carries m,n separately, never collapses to a function of n-m ⇒ no RoPE limit ⇒ graft

phase-resonance routing (as a routing rule) — contends with the §120-decided routing instead of composing with it; no limit recovers RoPE's q/k rotation ⇒ graft. §122 corrects §120 §4's imprecise wording: it is phase CODING, not phase-RESONANCE routing, that is position's spiking home

reduction_witness.statement: GPU byte-vocab RoPE is byte-equal to Phi(sigma->0), the zero-spike-time-jitter corner of the relative-phase family Phi(sigma). RoPE IS already a rotation = a phase; the GPU writes the angle m*theta by hand, a noise-free oscillator's phase advance equals it exactly.
reduction_witness.clean_single_parameter: sigma->0 only — cleaner than §120's reduction which needed k=T plus a hard->soft readout change
reduction_witness.s7_clean: generalisation not graft — byte-vocab RoPE is contained as a limit (RESEARCH.md §7 condition ② satisfied)
